patient.chief_complaint: Found unable to move left side on waking; last known well approximately 8 hours ago
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Esperanza Delgado is a 66-year-old right-handed Hispanic woman with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who is brought to the emergency department by her husband at 07:40 after he found her unable to rise from bed when he woke up. The husband reports that she was entirely at her baseline when they went to sleep at approximately 23:00 the previous evening — conversational, ambulating normally, and without any neurologic complaints. He awoke at approximately 07:10 and found her sitting on the edge of the bed, unable to stand, with her left arm hanging at her side and her eyes and head turned to the right. She was alert and speaking coherently but appeared unaware that anything was wrong with her left side. He immediately called 911. The patient herself denies any preceding symptoms — no headache, no visual symptoms, no palpitations, no chest pain, no tongue-biting or incontinence overnight. She is unaware of her left-sided weakness and reports feeling 'fine' other than being 'tired.' There was no witnessed seizure activity, no fever or recent illness, no trauma, no chiropractic manipulation. She has not taken any anticoagulants. She takes no aspirin or other antiplatelet agents. She has no prior history of stroke or TIA. Given that onset was unwitnessed during sleep, with the last known well established at bedtime approximately 8 hours before emergency department arrival, the clinical team must determine whether the patient qualifies for any acute reperfusion therapy. Standard IV tPA is not administered because onset time is unknown, placing the patient definitively outside the 4.5-hour window without imaging evidence of early onset. The attending neurologist activates the stroke team and orders urgent imaging including non-contrast CT, CTA, and CT perfusion to characterize the extent of ischemia and salvageable penumbra for potential extended-window mechanical thrombectomy decision.

results.title: Thrombectomy 6-24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct (DAWN Trial)
results.authors: Nogueira RG, Jadhav AP, et al.
results.key_finding: Mechanical thrombectomy 6-24 hours after last known well improved functional outcomes in patients with anterior circulation LVO, NIHSS >=10, and clinical-core mismatch (core volume <21 mL for age 80+ or NIHSS>=10; <31 mL for age <80 NIHSS>=10; <51 mL for age <80 NIHSS>=20). mRS 0-2 at 90 days: 49% thrombectomy vs 13% medical therapy.

results.title: Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging (DEFUSE-3)
results.authors: Albers GW, Marks MP, et al.
results.key_finding: Mechanical thrombectomy 6-16 hours after last known well improved outcomes when perfusion imaging showed: ischemic core volume <70 mL, mismatch ratio >=1.8, and mismatch volume >=15 mL. mRS 0-2 at 90 days: 45% thrombectomy vs 17% medical therapy. Imaging selection using automated software (RAPID) identifies favorable penumbra.

results.title: 2019 AHA/ASA Guidelines for Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke — Extended Window Recommendations
results.authors: Powers WJ, Rabinstein AA, et al.
results.key_finding: Mechanical thrombectomy is recommended (Class I, Level A) for eligible patients with anterior circulation LVO and NIHSS >=6 presenting 6-16 hours from last known well if DEFUSE-3 criteria are met, and 6-24 hours from last known well if DAWN criteria are met. IV tPA is not indicated when onset time is unknown outside imaging-guided criteria.

output.proposed: IV alteplase (tPA) 0.9 mg/kg IV versus mechanical thrombectomy — contraindication and interaction review for wake-up stroke with unknown onset
interactions: Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor): Concurrent ACE inhibitor therapy increases risk of orolingual angioedema with IV tPA — occurs in up to 5% of patients on ACE inhibitors. Requires careful monitoring during tPA infusion if administered.

Metformin: No direct pharmacokinetic interaction with tPA or contrast agents at standard doses; however, metformin should be held for 48 hours following iodinated contrast administration due to risk of contrast-induced nephropathy increasing metformin-associated lactic acidosis risk.
contraindications: Unknown time of onset (wake-up stroke): IV alteplase is contraindicated when last known well exceeds 4.5 hours unless DWI-FLAIR mismatch on MRI confirms likely onset within 4.5 hours. This patient's last known well is approximately 8 hours prior — standard IV tPA is not indicated without MRI tissue-clock evidence.

Blood pressure > 185/110 mmHg: Current BP 192/104 mmHg exceeds the maximum threshold for tPA eligibility. BP must be reduced to <185/110 mmHg and maintained stable before IV tPA administration, if otherwise eligible.
Recent use of anticoagulants with elevated drug levels: Not present in this patient — INR 1.0, no anticoagulant history.
Glucose < 50 mg/dL: Not applicable — glucose 188 mg/dL (hypoglycemia excluded as stroke mimic).
warnings: ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) confers increased orolingual angioedema risk if tPA is used — monitor closely.
Mechanical thrombectomy does not require IV tPA pre-treatment in all extended-window LVO patients; thrombectomy alone is appropriate when tPA is contraindicated.
Elevated admission glucose (188 mg/dL) is associated with worse outcomes after ischemic stroke regardless of reperfusion strategy; normoglycemia management is recommended.
No anticoagulant, recent surgery, or prior stroke within 3 months identified as additional contraindications.

sequence_constraints.reason: Non-contrast CT head must exclude intracranial hemorrhage before any thrombolytic agent is considered. The drug-interaction/contraindication check models the tPA eligibility decision and must follow CT confirmation of no hemorrhage.
CTA must first confirm LVO (right MCA M1 occlusion) before perfusion imaging is interpreted in the context of thrombectomy candidacy; perfusion is meaningful only when LVO is documented.
Glucose, INR/PTT, and platelet count must be reviewed before IV thrombolysis to exclude hypoglycemia mimic and coagulopathy contraindications.

critical_actions: Establish last known well time precisely — history confirms LKW at bedtime ~23:00, approximately 8 hours before ED arrival, placing the patient in the 6-24h extended window (DAWN) and 6-16h window (DEFUSE-3) for thrombectomy selection by perfusion imaging
Obtain non-contrast CT head FIRST to exclude intracranial hemorrhage before any reperfusion decision
Obtain CT angiography to document LVO (right MCA M1 occlusion) — LVO documentation is mandatory before mechanical thrombectomy

Obtain CT perfusion or MR perfusion to assess infarct core and penumbra — perfusion mismatch (core <70 mL, mismatch ratio >=1.8, mismatch volume >=15 mL) must be confirmed to meet DEFUSE-3 criteria for extended-window thrombectomy
Do NOT administer IV tPA based on unknown onset time alone — document that standard IV tPA is contraindicated when LKW exceeds 4.5 hours without MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch evidence of acute onset
Proceed to mechanical thrombectomy if DAWN/DEFUSE-3 imaging criteria are met — this case meets DEFUSE-3 criteria (core 18 mL < 70 mL, mismatch ratio 6.6 > 1.8, mismatch volume 100 mL > 15 mL)
Lower blood pressure to <185/110 mmHg before any thrombolytic administration if tPA is reconsidered; for thrombectomy-only, avoid excessive BP lowering that risks penumbral hypoperfusion
Initiate continuous cardiac monitoring and 48-hour Holter monitoring to detect paroxysmal AF as the embolic mechanism — initial ECG sinus rhythm does NOT exclude AF
Complete post-acute secondary workup: echocardiogram, carotid duplex, prolonged cardiac monitoring, lipid and diabetes optimization
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT administer IV tPA to this patient based solely on unknown onset time — standard IV tPA is contraindicated when last known well exceeds 4.5 hours and DWI-FLAIR mismatch confirming acute onset is absent

Do NOT declare the patient ineligible for all reperfusion therapy solely because onset is unknown — extended-window mechanical thrombectomy with perfusion imaging selection (DAWN/DEFUSE-3) is indicated when imaging criteria are met regardless of unknown clock time
Do NOT anchor on 'nothing can be done because she woke up with it' — wake-up stroke with favorable perfusion mismatch and LVO is a thrombectomy indication
Do NOT give IV tPA before non-contrast CT excludes intracranial hemorrhage
Do NOT aggressively lower blood pressure below 140-150 mmHg systolic in the acute phase — risks worsening perfusion to the large penumbra
Do NOT skip CTA before thrombectomy — LVO must be documented prior to endovascular intervention

Do NOT skip perfusion imaging in the extended window — core size and mismatch ratio determine eligibility; proceeding without perfusion imaging risks treating patients with large cores who are unlikely to benefit
key_reasoning_points: Wake-up stroke with unknown onset time places the patient outside the standard IV tPA window (4.5h); however, unknown onset time does NOT preclude mechanical thrombectomy in the extended window when perfusion imaging demonstrates favorable mismatch

DAWN (6-24h) and DEFUSE-3 (6-16h) trials established that imaging-based patient selection — small infarct core with large salvageable penumbra — identifies patients who benefit from mechanical thrombectomy far beyond the conventional time window

This case meets DEFUSE-3 criteria: ischemic core 18 mL (below 70 mL threshold), mismatch ratio 6.6 (above 1.8 threshold), mismatch volume 100 mL (above 15 mL threshold) — mechanical thrombectomy is indicated

Laterality check: right MCA M1 occlusion causes contralateral left-sided deficits (left dense hemiplegia, left hemisensory loss, left neglect, left hemianopia) and ipsilateral gaze deviation to the RIGHT (toward the lesion) — there is NO aphasia because the right hemisphere is non-dominant for language in this right-handed patient

The 'wake-up stroke / nothing to do' anchoring heuristic is the primary red herring — the correct clinical response is to proceed urgently to perfusion imaging and thrombectomy evaluation, not to default to supportive care
FLAIR-positive DWI infarct confirms lesion age >4.5 hours, excluding MRI-guided tPA (WAKE-UP criteria); this reinforces that thrombectomy, not tPA, is the appropriate reperfusion strategy

Left atrial enlargement on initial ECG plus newly detected paroxysmal AF on Holter monitoring identifies a likely cardioembolic mechanism — anticoagulation (not antiplatelet) becomes the secondary prevention cornerstone once hemorrhagic transformation risk is acceptable

red_herrings.data_point: Wake-up stroke — last known well approximately 8 hours before ED arrival (bedtime 23:00, found 07:10)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude that all reperfusion therapies are contraindicated because onset time is unknown and the conventional 4.5h IV tPA window has been exceeded — 'nothing to offer, supportive care only'
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Unknown onset time excludes standard IV tPA but does NOT preclude extended-window mechanical thrombectomy; DAWN (6-24h) and DEFUSE-3 (6-16h) use perfusion imaging mismatch criteria rather than clock time alone — favorable mismatch (core 18 mL, mismatch ratio 6.6) qualifies this patient for thrombectomy

red_herrings.data_point: Normal sinus rhythm on initial 12-lead ECG
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude that cardiac arrhythmia is not the embolic source and skip extended cardiac monitoring
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm on a single resting ECG does NOT exclude paroxysmal AF; left atrial enlargement on the same ECG is a structural marker for AF risk and mandates prolonged monitoring — Holter monitoring subsequently identifies two AF episodes

metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle — wake-up stroke with unknown last-known-well (LKW) creates anchoring toward 'no reperfusion possible'; the critical insight is that DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria enable extended-window mechanical thrombectomy using perfusion mismatch (small core 18 mL, large penumbra 118 mL, mismatch ratio 6.6) despite unknown onset. IV tPA is contraindicated. Laterality is right MCA M1 occlusion causing left hemiplegia, left neglect, and rightward gaze deviation with no aphasia. Paroxysmal AF identified only on Holter monitoring despite initial sinus ECG.
clinical_pearls: Wake-up stroke does not mean 'no treatment' — the extended thrombectomy window (DAWN 6-24h, DEFUSE-3 6-16h) was specifically designed for unknown-onset presentations with favorable perfusion mismatch
The critical metric is not the clock: it is the ratio of ischemic core to salvageable penumbra. Core <70 mL + mismatch ratio >1.8 + mismatch volume >15 mL are the DEFUSE-3 imaging thresholds

Right MCA M1 occlusion produces leftward deficits (left hemiplegia, left neglect, left hemianopia) and RIGHTWARD cortical gaze deviation — do not confuse with left MCA stroke where gaze deviates left and aphasia is expected
Left atrial enlargement on the admission ECG is a structural risk marker for paroxysmal AF; normal sinus rhythm on a resting tracing does not exclude AF as the embolic source
case_body_concerns: Mock-server note: This case uses two sequential order_ct_scan calls (non-contrast primary, CTA as followup trigger 'request_ct_angiography') and one order_advanced_imaging call (perfusion_MRI as followup trigger 'request_perfusion_imaging'). The mock server must route the CTA and perfusion as separate followup_outputs keyed by their trigger_action strings, not to the initial_tool_outputs.ct or initial_tool_outputs.advanced_imaging slots. The initial_tool_outputs.ct is populated with the non-contrast result.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Wake-up stroke with unknown LKW anchoring red herring, required perfusion-mismatch reasoning for extended-window thrombectomy (DAWN/DEFUSE-3), multiple required tools (CT x2, CTP, labs, ECG, literature, drug check, MRI, echo, Holter, carotid duplex), paroxysmal AF only on Holter not initial ECG.
